todaysEvents.summary: US pauses Iran strikes for 3rd day; Omani talks
todaysEvents.delta: Neutral: After 13 consecutive nights of US strikes over 1,000 targets, the Trump administration paused operations on Jul 25. The pause entered its 3rd day Jul 27 with no US strikes and no Iranian retaliatory attacks. An Omani delegation arrived in Tehran for talks on Hormuz passage mechanisms (Al Jazeera, Jul 24-27). UN Ambassador Waltz: 'giving diplomacy some space' (CBS, Jul 26). Diplomatic window fragile but open.

todaysEvents.summary: Tanker explodes after hitting mine in Hormuz
todaysEvents.delta: Up: An oil tanker attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz exploded after hitting naval mines, Iranian officials confirmed Jul 27. Iran warned that any ship attempting passage must be in 'full coordination' otherwise Iran cannot guarantee safety (Al Jazeera, Jul 27). Incident underscores continued danger in the waterway despite pause in airstrikes.

todaysEvents.summary: Brent recedes from $100+ to $91.91 on pause
todaysEvents.delta: Down: Brent briefly crossed $100/bbl intraday Jul 24 (ICE $100.91 open, $101.16 high) before closing at $96.78 (Yahoo Finance). With the US strike pause entering day 3 and diplomatic channels active, Brent eased to $91.91 (Jul 27, +0.99% intraday). TTF rose to €63.58 (Jul 24, +2.71%) on sustained LNG supply concerns. Tail reduced from 70% to 45% on diplomatic opening.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: The Omani-led diplomatic channel gains traction as both sides observe a pause in hostilities. Diplomatic talks produce a framework for phased Hormuz reopening and restoration of the June MOU ceasefire. Brent settles toward $80-90/bbl as risk premium deflates. Probability raised to 20% reflecting the active diplomatic window and mutual pause.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Pause collapses after talks fail to make progress on core issues (Hormuz control, nuclear program, blockade conditions). US resumes intermittent strikes; Iran retaliates at a constrained tempo. Hormuz remains effectively closed with occasional tanker transits. Brent trades $90-110/bbl, TTF stays elevated. Probability increased to 35% reflecting the fragility of the pause and unresolved core issues.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Diplomacy fails and the pause breaks down. US strikes resume at scale, potentially targeting nuclear sites. Iran escalates with full-scale offensive ops. Kuwait water infrastructure already damaged; GCC states face sustained attacks. Brent spikes $100-130+/bbl, JKM above $30/MMBtu. Probability reduced from 70% to 45% reflecting the diplomatic opening but still elevated given the underlying conflict intensity.
